piezas.titulo: Cellular and mitochondrial correlates of regional glucose metabolism in the human cortex
piezas.resumenOriginal: Regional differences in human brain glucose metabolism reflect local energy demands, but their cellular and mitochondrial determinants remain unclear. We combined [18F]FDG positron emission tomography in healthy human participants with estimates of cellular composition and mitochondrial density to unravel (sub)cellular correlates of heterogeneity in brain glucose metabolism. By correcting for RNA content and differential gene expression due to postmortem sampling, we addressed methodological shortcomings in multimodal neuroimaging integration. We introduce transcriptionally derived cytoarchitectonic maps of the human cortex that are consistent with histological findings, providing a biologically grounded framework for relating in vivo neuroimaging signals. Accordingly, mitochondrial distribution showed strong association with the intrinsic energy requirements at resting state. In contrast, relations between metabolism and neuronal composition were driven by sensory input and mitochondria-sparse thin-axon neurons, suggesting that stimulation-induced energy demand is met rather by neuronal processes that are independent of mitochondrial abundance to maintain efficient information processing.

piezas.titulo: From a surgeon's stroke to a third hemisphere—The auxilium architecture for brain restoration and extension
piezas.resumenOriginal: A surgeon was exercising on a stationary bicycle when he had a large ischemic left middle cerebral artery territory stroke, complicated by hemorrhagic transformation requiring hemicraniectomy and cranioplasty. He developed right-sided spastic hemiplegia and a mixed aphasia. This paper takes that case as its anchor to pose the question: beyond improving residual function, what would it mean to restore cognitive function that was lost so that the person fully returns to their pre-stroke baseline? Existing brain-computer interfaces rely on the person having an intact cortical substrate for intended movement and speech. Here we propose the Auxilium, a brain restoration architecture for the situation where that substrate is no longer present: an extracranial auxiliary brain system, agnostic to its substrate, that connects to a person's residual cortex through whatever input-output technology proves most appropriate, and that supplies, in parallel and in real time, new substrate, whether biological or synthetic. We address an assumption of brain-computer interface development, that throughput is the binding constraint. Linking a kHz brain to MHz digital does not impart the higher clock speed, because the limitation lies not in the port but in the architecture of the entire brain and body imparted by evolution. We posit that the substrate of canonical circuits and their integration areas is essential, and the Auxilium can be understood as restoring both connectivity (linkage between disconnected areas) and computation (information generation capability of a volume of neural tissue). We propose a near-term de-risking pipeline using stereoelectroencephalography during surgical epilepsy evaluation, comparing extracranial modules spanning threshold rules, PID controllers, expert systems, artificial neural networks, neuromorphic devices, and biological specimens, each linked in real time to a participant serving as their own control on naturalistic tasks. If ports alone restore the lost function, the requirement is routing connectivity. If performance improves only when the module supplies its own dynamics, the requirement is computational substrate. We expect the answer to depend on how much tissue was lost, how quickly, and on the individual's reserve, and we treat routing and substrate as endpoints of a continuum to be mapped empirically.

piezas.titulo: How Wikipedia’s Editors Keep the Online Encyclopedia Human-Written
piezas.resumenOriginal: Ellia Lebleu is a founding member of the WikiProject AI Cleanup , a volunteer effort launched in 2023 to find and remove AI-generated material from Wikipedia that breaks the website’s guidelines. When the cleanup began, AI writing was often betrayed by conspicuous clichés. Today, the project’s volunteers are developing tools to detect subtler forms of machine-generated content and debating AI’s role in the world’s most widely used encyclopedia. When did you realize Wikipedia had a problem with AI-generated material? Ellia Lebleu: It was around December 2023. A few other editors and I were chatting on Wikipedia’s Discord server, and we had all seen very strange articles with the same odd characteristics. They repeated phrases like “stands as a testament” or “rich cultural heritage.” They sometimes had conclusion sections, or sections called “Why is this important?” That was very typical of ChatGPT in 2023 and early 2024 but very odd for Wikipedia articles—and very easy to spot. Then I decided, let’s create an official project on Wikipedia so more people can deal with this. Ellia Lebleu Ellia Lebleu is a founding member of the WikiProject AI Cleanup. Lebleu is pursuing a Ph.D. in AI at the Inria Center of the University of Rennes , part of France’s national research institute for digital science and technology. How do editors spot AI-generated writing today? Lebleu: By 2025, the signs of AI writing were becoming subtler and more structural. For example, AI loves the “rule of three,” negative parallelisms, and other structures of speech that aren’t conclusive by themselves but become meaningful as they accumulate. We also look beyond the article. If someone writes five articles of thousands of words each in 5 minutes, there is reason to suspect AI. Does the AI problem just appear in the main text, or also in citations? Lebleu: Fake or misleading citations have become a major worry. Sometimes an AI hallucinates a citation entirely, although that’s much rarer today because of retrieval-augmented generation that allows the AI to find sources. More often, it finds a real source but gets its content completely wrong. AI citations that don’t actually support what is being written are extremely commonplace. English Wikipedia recently prohibited editors from using LLMs to generate articles. How much AI-generated content is still getting through? Lebleu: I’ve been working with [AI-detection company] Pangram to estimate the proportion of AI-generated content. I tested it on Wikipedia content from before ChatGPT and found no false positives, so its results provide a very conservative lower bound. In late 2025, it flagged perhaps 20 percent of new articles and drafts as AI-generated. In early 2026, that went down to 15 or 16 percent. But we don’t yet know whether that’s because our recent policies have had an effect or because models are getting more powerful and Pangram hasn’t had time to adapt. Is Wikipedia using AI to combat AI? Lebleu: Another Wikipedia editor has made an AI source verifier, which goes through the sources on a page and checks whether they match the claims. Since it is itself an AI model, there is no guarantee that it will be correct every time. But if you want something that works at scale and filters out obvious cases, it’s a good first step. The Wikimedia Foundation is also working on a tool called Paste Check , which can flag text pasted directly from some AI chatbots. And we’ve seen Claude sometimes say, “I can’t write a Wikipedia article; it would go against Wikipedia’s policies.” If all major AI companies implemented that kind of prompt refusal, it wouldn’t solve the problem entirely, because there are still open-weight models that can be tweaked to avoid restrictions. But it would help with people who use commercial models and aren’t especially familiar with the technology. Can you tell if the rule prohibiting AI writing is working? Lebleu: It’s still a little early to tell. We see possible effects, such as prompt refusal and the apparent slight drop in AI-generated content. But again, we don’t yet know if that is because models are getting better or because beginners are learning the rules. The vast majority of AI-generated content is submitted by beginner editors, so we’ve made many efforts to make the rule very visible in welcome messages, editing help, and advice. What if AI becomes capable of writing truly reliable Wikipedia articles? Lebleu: That’s one of the big questions we’re facing. When the guideline was passed, it was for very practical reasons: We were flooded with AI content, we didn’t have good tools, and we needed to put a stop to it. But since then, it has taken on a more philosophical dimension. Many people have called Wikipedia “the last good place on the internet.” Being a place that was, in theory, free from AI slop has become part of Wikipedia’s identity. A lot of Wikipedia’s communication is now centered on the idea that we’re a human-written encyclopedia. Even AI companies find that interesting. It can be valuable to have a purely human-written corpus on which to [train] AI systems. The fact that Wikipedia is still that, and will remain that for at least the near future, makes it a precious resource that isn’t replicated anywhere else. But will the people who read and contribute to Wikipedia want it to become partially AI-generated if that makes it more comprehensive? We could preserve Wikipedia’s identity as a human-written corpus while also offering an AI-assisted option. Has Wikipedia reckoned with the idea of “Google Zero”—a possible future in which websites no longer get traffic from Google search? Lebleu: If everything goes through AI search and websites plummet to zero visibility, how do we expose Wikipedia and show that it can be edited and that people can still contribute? Wikipedia is frequently cited in [Google’s] AI Overviews, but users may only see an AI answer citing Wikipedia. They may not realize that Wikipedia is a living project they can edit and contribute to. The Wikimedia Foundation is working on an attribution framework that could give AI users more information about the article [being cited]: when it was last edited, how comprehensive it is, whether editors have flagged problems, and perhaps even a call to action. In the future, readers might even contribute through AI models: “The AI cited Wikipedia, but there seems to be an error. Can I make an edit request and add this other source I found?” I can see a very strong symbiotic relationship between Wikipedia and AI models in the future. I don’t see Wikipedia disappearing, but I can see it taking a very different shape. Yesterday, AI was something to clean up. Today, it’s a tool to help us with the cleanup. Tomorrow, it will be the air we breathe. A condensed version of this article appears in the November 2026 print issue as “Ellia Lebleu.”

piezas.titulo: "It cannot depend solely on the parents"-professionals' perspectives on patient journeys of children with chronic conditions across health and social care in Germany.
piezas.resumenOriginal: Purpose Professionals in healthcare, social services and the education system are confronted with a growing number of children with chronic conditions. Complex treatment plans, care coordination and cross-system care needs result in additional demands on professionals. This study aimed to explore professionals' perspectives on the patient journeys of children with chronic conditions in Germany and identify opportunities to improve care. Methods This qualitative study used semi-structured interviews conducted from May 2023 to February 2024. A purposive sample of professionals working with children with chronic conditions (attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, autism spectrum disorder, developmental disorders, cerebral palsy, bronchial asthma, type 1 diabetes) was recruited from the health, social care, and education systems in Germany. Sampling was guided by an assessment of thematic saturation. Data were analysed using structuring qualitative content analysis. Results Twenty-two professionals participated, including physicians (n = 7), therapists (n = 8) and social workers and counsellors (n = 7). Care was perceived as fragmented, difficult to navigate, and poorly coordinated across health, social care, and education systems. Key barriers included long waiting times, unclear care pathways, and limited interprofessional communication. Greater difficulties in navigating care and support were perceived among families facing socioeconomic disadvantage or language barriers. Conclusion Professionals perceived current care structures as insufficiently meeting the needs of children with chronic conditions, particularly where families face greater barriers to navigating services. Strengthening cross-system coordination and accessibility may improve patient journeys. Future research should examine how barriers vary according to socioeconomic circumstances and across stages of the patient journey and evaluate condition-independent approaches to improving care. Trial registration This study was registered in the German Clinical Trials Register, ID: DRKS00032139, on 07 November 2023. What is known • Research on patient journeys of children with chronic conditions has primarily focused on individual, often rare, conditions. • Evidence spanning multiple chronic conditions and the healthcare, social services, and education systems remains highly limited. What is new • Drawing on diverse professionals' perspectives, this study provides a cross-system, cross-condition view of paediatric patient journeys. • It identifies common barriers to care coordination and access across systems and diagnoses, highlighting actionable opportunities for integrated care.

piezas.titulo: Lifestyle Documentation in Therapy Evaluations for Autistic Children: A Lexicon-Based Analysis of Electronic Health Records.
piezas.resumenOriginal: BackgroundWhole person health (WPH) is a multidimensional construct encompassing, physical, and mental health along with relational constructs such as social health that are deeply tied to well-being. Autistic individuals report an overall lower quality of life, but the extent to which these issues are addressed during therapy evaluations has not been examined systematically.MethodologyIn this retrospective, cross-sectional study, we employ a rule-based NLP/lexicon-based approach to examine the areas of focus of therapy evaluations documented by occupational therapy, physical therapy (PT), and speech-language pathology (SLP) professionals. Using electronic health records for children aged 2 to 18 diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) (n = 5619 evaluation reports of n = 2021 unique patients), we classified health records based on the domains addressed.ResultsAcross notes, nutrition had the highest average degree of documentation ( M = 2.14), compared to activity ( M = 0.91), followed by wellness ( M = 0.66), and sleep ( M = 0.39). In occupational therapy, wellness was the most common (77.62% of notes), followed by physical activity (76.49% of notes), nutrition management (73.33% of notes), and sleep (34.97% of notes). The overall area under the curve (AUC) from the receiver operating characteristic analysis is 0.89.ConclusionsWhile it is encouraging that most evaluations addressed nutrition or physical activity, the near absence of attention to sleep represents a critical gap in care. Given sleep's foundational role in overall health and daily functioning, its omission is particularly concerning. Occupational therapists and interdisciplinary rehabilitation teams should more deliberately integrate WPH frameworks into their evaluations.

piezas.titulo: Application of weighted gene co-expression network analysis to explore the targets of treadmill training in rats with spinal cord injury
piezas.resumenOriginal: BackgroundSpinal cord injury (SCI) describes any damage to the spinal cord that results in a loss of function. With these injuries being commonly treated with subsequent treadmill training (TM), this study aimed to reveal the mechanisms facilitating TM-mediated rehabilitation following a SCI.MethodsDifferentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified and then subjected to a weighted gene co-expression network analysis to identify TM-associated modules. Co-expression network construction, functional annotation, protein–protein interaction (PPI) network, and transcription factor (TF)-miRNA-target regulatory network were then conducted. We established an SCI rat model and validated key RNAs using reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR). Predicted interactions between miR-135a-5p and JAK2 and STAT1 were tested using dual-luciferase reporter assay.ResultsTotal 640 and 877 genes separately differentially expressed in SCI 8d + TM vs. SCI 8d and SCI 14d + TM vs. SCI 14d comparison groups were screened and merged as the DEGs, which were further narrowed to four TM-associated modules linked to the glutamatergic synapse and ribosome biogenesis pathways. PPI network evaluations identified v-Akt murine thymoma viral oncogene homolog 1 (AKT1), Janus kinase 2 (JAK2), tumor necrosis factor (TNF), and signal transducer and activator of transcription 1 (STAT1) as hub nodes. JAK2 and STAT1 were also shown to have interactions in module b. TF-miRNA-target regulatory network revealed that both STAT1 and JAK2 were targets of miR-135a. RT-qPCR results confirmed upregulation of AKT1 and STAT1 and downregulation of JAK2, TNF and miR-135a after TM. piezas.titulo: Astrocytic ablation of truncated TrkB receptors reduces amyloid plaques and prevents synaptic loss in 5xFAD mice
piezas.resumenOriginal: Brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) is essential for nervous system development and function and exerts its effects primarily through the tropomyosin receptor kinase B (TrkB). The Ntrk2 gene encodes a full-length receptor (TrkB.FL) and two truncated isoforms (TrkB.T1 and TrkB.T2, collectively TrkB.T) that lack the intracellular tyrosine kinase domain. TrkB.T is expressed predominantly in astrocytes and is thought to inhibit BDNF-TrkB.FL signaling by sequestering BDNF and forming signaling-deficient heterodimers with TrkB.FL. Here, we investigated whether selective ablation of astrocytic TrkB.T could ameliorate Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology by enhancing endogenous BDNF-TrkB.FL signaling. Astrocyte-specific deletion of the Ntrk2 gene at 5 weeks of age reduced cortical TrkB.T expression by more than 80% without affecting TrkB.FL levels. TrkB.T ablation increased the size of Bassoon-positive presynaptic active zones, consistent with enhanced BDNF-TrkB.FL signaling. Remarkably, astrocytic TrkB.T ablation reduced {beta}-amyloid plaque burden by more than 60% in the cortex, hippocampus, and subiculum of 6-month-old 5xFAD mice, despite having no detectable effect on microgliosis or astrogliosis. Furthermore, TrkB.T ablation prevented reductions in the density and size of PSD-95-positive postsynaptic sites in the cortex and hippocampus of 5xFAD mice at 1 year old. Together, these findings identify astrocytic TrkB.T as an important regulator of amyloid pathology and synaptic integrity in an AD mouse model. Our results suggest that selectively reducing TrkB.T expression represents a promising therapeutic strategy to enhance endogenous neuroprotective BDNF-TrkB.FL signaling, reduce amyloid pathology, and preserve synaptic integrity in AD.

piezas.titulo: State-dependent responses of emotional brain networks in high myopia under blurred vision: a shift towards dorsal stream and cross-modal processing
piezas.resumenOriginal: PurposeReliable sensory input plays a vital role in shaping emotional experience, however, how the brain modulates the formation of emotion under chronic visual degradation remains unclear. Using high myopia (HM) as a natural model of sustained blur, this study investigated state-dependent responses of emotional brain networks during blurred movie viewing.MethodsTwenty-four participants with high myopia (HM) were tested without optical correction, comparing with normal vision (NV) controls from previous research. All participants watched thriller and scenic movie clips twice over one week during fMRI. Intra-subject synchrony and seed-based functional connectivity analyses focused on the amygdala and visual processing streams.ResultsCompared to NV controls, the HM group exhibited reduced intra-subject synchrony in visual cortices but increased synchrony in the primary auditory cortex, indicating cross-modal compensatory enhancement. During threat processing, HM participants showed strengthened and stable functional connectivity between the amygdala and the dorsal visual stream. For non-threatening content, this enhanced connectivity initially involved both dorsal and ventral stream but persisted selectively in the dorsal stream upon repeated viewing.ConclusionSustained visual blur elicits a perceptual-state-dependent functional response in emotional networks, characterized by heightened cross-modal auditory integration and an increased recruitment of the visual dorsal stream during blurred viewing. These findings highlight the brain’s immediate compensatory mechanisms under conditions of ambiguous visual input.

piezas.titulo: Neurophysiological dynamics related to perception, action, and language in schizophrenia.
piezas.resumenOriginal: Schizophrenia disrupts both how people perceive the world and how they express and act on their thoughts, yet these symptoms are usually studied separately. Using magnetoencephalography during multisensory and motor tasks, we tested whether reduced event-related beta-band (15 to 30 hertz) modulation, a signal implicated in predictive control, provides a candidate neural marker across these domains. Compared to healthy individuals, patients showed diminished beta changes during sensory processing and movement completion, suggesting reduced flexibility in updating internal models. This neural pattern covaried with audiovisual simultaneity-judgment behavior, disorganized natural speech, and greater clinical severity. These findings suggest that distributed beta modulation may serve as a candidate cross-domain marker associated with perceptual, motor, and language disturbances in schizophrenia, motivating future studies that directly test predictive updating mechanisms.

piezas.titulo: The Feasibility of Using Virtual Reality With Debriefing as a Treatment Modality for Chronic Pain.
piezas.resumenOriginal: ImportanceChronic pain is a leading cause of disability. Traditional rehabilitation approaches may not produce meaningful functional improvement, necessitating innovative approaches.ObjectiveTo assess the feasibility and acceptability of integrating fully immersive virtual reality (FIVR) and debriefing into occupational therapy (OT) for chronic pain management. We hypothesized that FIVR plus debriefing (IVRSOT) would improve pain, fear of movement, and confidence compared to standard OT (SOT).DesignIn this mixed methods feasibility study, participants were randomized to SOT or IVRSOT. Data were analyzed using nonparametric statistics and content analysis.SettingOutpatient interdisciplinary pain clinic using a biopsychosocial model.ParticipantsAdults with chronic pain, with 31 enrolled and 16 having data suitable for analysis.Outcomes and MeasuresPain intensity, pain interference, kinesiophobia, self-efficacy, and social functioning were assessed using validated tools.ResultsIVRSOT participants showed significant improvement in pain self-efficacy, fatigue, and pain interference, accompanied by a decline in physical function; between group comparisons for physical function and social role participation favored SOT. Qualitative data revealed enhanced engagement, insight, and functional carryover.Conclusion and RelevanceFIVR with debriefing is a feasible and engaging approach for chronic pain intervention, with the potential to enhance self-efficacy and functional outcomes.

piezas.titulo: From hours to days: prolonging the functional viability of acute brain slices to >36 h
piezas.resumenOriginal: We have developed an experimental protocol for acute brain slices of juvenile and adult mice which, in our hands, enables whole-cell patch-clamp experiments on healthy neurons with intact electrophysiological characteristics for more than 36 hours after preparation. This drastically expands the conventional viability window of brain slices of 8-12 hours, using only standard laboratory equipment and procedures. We successfully applied this protocol to evaluate neurons of the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), motor cortex (M1/M2), globus pallidus (GP), and thalamic reticular nucleus (TRN) of mice aged P11 to ~2 years postnatal, demonstrating the robustness of our method. By prolonging the usability of the preparation, this procedure a) reduces the number of animals used per study, b) yields healthy brain slices also from adult animals, c) allows prolonged experimental procedures, and d) reduces material cost and preparation effort for the experimenter.
